history.idea: Replace random order with a target-similarity filter. (1) Exact-dedupe docs by normalized text hash (keep first). (2) Fit a TfidfVectorizer on character n-grams (analyzer='char_wb', ngram_range=(1,4), sublinear_tf=True, max_features=200k, each doc truncated to its first 3000 chars) on target_sample + a seeded 6000-doc random pool subset; train LogisticRegression (C=1, class_weight='balanced') with target_sample as positives and the random pool subset as negatives; score every pool doc by decision_function. (3) Add cheap junk guards: drop docs with <200 chars, or with unique-word ratio <0.2, or non-ASCII/non-alpha-space char fraction >0.4. (4) Sort surviving docs by score descending, estimate tokens as len(text)/4 (or tiktoken gpt2 if within time), and take top-scoring docs until about 1.0 T tokens are accumulated (if fewer than 0.5 T have score > 0, still fill up to 1.0 T by score order). (5) Shuffle the selected indices with random.Random(CURATE_SEED) and return them.
